<h1 class="title-h1 eac-page-title">59 new Erasmus+ projects selected on international cooperation in vocational education and training</h1>
<span><span>holbobe</span></span>
<span><time datetime="2026-10-09T12:49:22+02:00" title="Friday, October 9, 2026 - 12:49">Fri, 10/09/2026 - 12:49</time>
</span>
<div class="ecl"><h2>Capacity building in vocational education and training</h2><p>Funded projects on capacity building in vocational education and training (VET) support cooperation between European and non-European VET organisations and close the gaps between VET and market opportunities. They are mostly targeting countries outside Europe.</p><h2>Commitment to global partnerships</h2><p>More than 28 million Euros has been allocated to the 59 new projects, covering 68 countries and selected from a record number of eligible evaluated proposals.</p><p>The projects aim to create bridges to advance VET systems globally through knowledge exchange and mutual growth. They show again how the Erasmus+ programme is committed to building global partnerships beyond the EU.</p><p>Partnerships involve European VET organisations and their counterparts in the Western Balkans, South and East neighbouring countries, Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America and the Caribbeans.</p><h2>2026 highlights</h2><h3>Cross-border digital innovation</h3><p>Projects are pioneering the next generation of digital learning tools by sharing technological advancements and best practices in digital education to benefit learners across continents.</p><h3>Sustainability beyond borders</h3><p>Addressing global challenges requires global solutions. Projects focused on green skills development are engaging international partners to create a more sustainable future. This includes joint programmes on renewable energy technologies, sustainable agricultural practices, and eco-conscious entrepreneurship.</p><h3>Strengthening global networks</h3><p>The collaborative nature of these projects strengthens global networks of educators, VET learners, and industry experts. They provide a platform for exchanging ideas, methodologies and resources, enriching the educational experiences of all participants.</p><h2>Impact and expectations</h2><p>Collaborations are expected to improve the employability and skill levels of learners and raise trainers’ competencies both within Europe and in partner countries. By aligning vocational training with global industry trends and labour market needs, the projects contribute to economic growth and social development across continents.</p><h2>Project examples</h2><ul><li data-list-item-id="e40b1df40d17cd352df52167a33365e04">Strengthening Vocational Education and Training for flood management, climate resilience and crisis preparedness in Latin America</li><li data-list-item-id="e5514f0b5d7fee3ea4e2678b34ed0153d">Transition towards a reconstruction-ready VET Teaching workforce in Ukraine</li><li data-list-item-id="e714879f560455a320251419d0ff7214c">Strengthening VET in Green Entrepreneurship for Young Women in the Fashion Industry in Tunisia and Morocco</li><li data-list-item-id="e6aa3da10f40feba048280886bdd8ffe6">Ophthalmic Nurse Technician Training in Sub-Saharan Africa</li><li data-list-item-id="ef5b4dde0d47fe93c763c79946cb3d17e">Transforming TVET for Waste-to-Energy Skills in East Africa</li><li data-list-item-id="ebec65cc22dc3c2bf432ef9a35955ecd6">Drone Pilot Training for Precision Irrigation and Water-Smart Agriculture in the Western Balkans</li><li data-list-item-id="ee51c6050bcc869adb4cac83393660aee">Digital Quality Assurance and Graduate Tracking for Labour Market Responsive VET in Albania</li></ul></div>
<div class="ecl-u-type-bold ecl-u-mb-m">Intro Text</div><div class="eac-hero"><p>Newly selected international partnerships aim to align vocational training with industry trends and labour market needs, and help learners across Europe and beyond gain more skills that employers are seeking.</p></div>

  <title>European Student Card Initiative at EAIE 2026 in Glasgow - main highlights</title>
  <link>https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/european-student-card-initiative/news/european-student-card-initiative-at-eaie-2026-in-glasgow-main-highlights</link>
  <description>
<h1 class="title-h1 eac-page-title">European Student Card Initiative at EAIE 2026 in Glasgow - main highlights</h1>
<span><span>holbobe</span></span>
<span><time datetime="2026-09-30T09:11:45+02:00" title="Wednesday, September 30, 2026 - 09:11">Wed, 09/30/2026 - 09:11</time>
</span>
<div class="ecl"><p>EAIE 2026 took place from 8 to 11 September, with this year’s theme being “The Rhythm of Revolution”. ESCI featured in five activities: two sessions in the main conference programme and three mini-sessions at the European Commission stand.</p><h2>Shaping the next phase of the ESCI</h2><p>The session “What’s next for the European Student Card Initiative?” brought together Victor Aguilar Mendez from the European Commission, Harpa Sif Arnarsdóttir from RANNIS and Sergi Martínez Rigol from the University of Barcelona to discuss the roadmap beyond 2027.</p><p>The discussion highlighted three main points:</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ec04a08fab5a0a15faf6d0537ff166c1e"><strong>Build on strong foundations</strong>. Participants welcomed the ambition to further simplify student mobility and emphasised the importance of building on the progress already achieved. They also noted that digital transformation involves more than technical connections, requiring aligned processes, staff capacity and resources.</li><li data-list-item-id="ec8f6683d0b4c64c36760e88ede263ada"><strong>Give institutions clarity and time to prepare</strong>. Participants highlighted the value of clear information on the <a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/european-student-card-initiative/about/esci-2028-2034/continuity-and-preparation?">future scope of ESCI+</a>, practical implications and transition arrangements. The European Commission indicated that 2028 and 2029 are envisaged as transition years.</li><li data-list-item-id="e8a2629faf233a9053a3e7c84c25e2248"><strong>Broaden engagement beyond international relations and IT teams</strong>. Participants highlighted the value of involving university leadership, national authorities, governance bodies and research and education networks.</li></ul><h2>Practical exchange at the European Commission stand</h2><p>Three mini-sessions created space for practical discussion and peer exchange at the European Commission stand:</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ea46800eaa0963f636bf8742a636fe844"><strong>Digital Officers and ESCI Champions</strong>: “Meet and Greet” explored different opportunities for close collaboration and participants discussed faster communication channels, technical sub-groups and ways to strengthen the community of practitioners.</li><li data-list-item-id="e722608eb7be29071793748afb04db370"><strong>ESCI+ timeline: what to expect and when</strong>, focused on preparations in 2026 and plans for 2027. Participants asked for timely communication, hands-on training, transition arrangements and support to integrate future developments with existing systems.</li><li data-list-item-id="e4abeb75d22c4e87d628dd3a9174bdc0a"><strong>How to issue your first European Student Card</strong> introduced the practical tools available to card issuers, including the ESC Router and the ESC Service Manager for listing services available to ESC holders.</li></ul><h2>Poster session: “The European Student Card: Bridging borders for students”</h2><p>The poster attracted strong interest, with ESCI representatives Elodie Ham (EACEA) and Deborah Arnold (NTT DATA) engaging with participants on the ESCI components and discussing the implications of the ESCI+ timeline with those already involved in the initiative as well as with potential newcomers.</p><h2>Session by ESCI Champions: “Erasmus Without Paper: Getting on board with the digitisation of Erasmus+"&nbsp;</h2></div>
<div class="ecl-u-type-bold ecl-u-mb-m">Intro Text</div><div class="eac-hero"><p>We joined more than 7,300 international education professionals from over 100 countries in Glasgow to discuss what comes next for the European Student Card Initiative and share practical guidance with institutions.</p></div>

                                            <div class="slider-text-body eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text">
            <div><p>In addition to the sessions organised by the European Commission, <a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/european-student-card-initiative/community/esci-champions?">ESCI Champions</a> (Kristin Anderson, University of Galway, Ireland, Katherine Bruun Funch, University of Copenhagen , Denmark, and Dana Rocklin, Stockholm University, Sweden) ran a practical workshop entitled "Erasmus Without Paper: Getting on board with the digitisation of Erasmus+". The session was very well-attended and enabled participants to share good practices and challenges in using different mobility management systems, including the EWP Dashboard.</p></div>

  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2>Looking ahead</h2><p>Preparation for ESCI+ will continue in close dialogue with all stakeholders via support and user training planned for 2027, helping institutions build on existing progress and prepare for the next phase at a sustainable pace.</p><p>The discussions in Glasgow demonstrated a shared commitment to making student mobility simpler, more connected and more accessible. The next steps will focus on supporting higher education institutions as they continue this work.</p></div>

Factories have invested billions in automation, yet production is still steered largely by people. Every night, a plan is computed for the next day, and the first disruption makes it obsolete. From then on, planners and shift leads juggle dependencies by hand. That is expensive, rarely optimal, and wastes much of what these factories were built for.

We are building the layer that takes over when the plan gets disrupted. It connects to factory data, models production, detects disruptions and bottlenecks as they emerge, simulates responses and recommends the best one.

planqor.ai was born on the shop floor. Our founding team brings deep production expertise, strong industry networks. We have the runway to build deliberately and the experience of people who have built and scaled successful companies before.   • Integration: Connect native C++ components, factory data, and product workflows into one coherent system.

  • Infrastructure: Own CI/CD, containers, deployment, observability, and the supporting services we need.

  • The team: Grow into leading software engineering at planqor.ai as we scale: hiring, mentoring, and setting direction.

You set your own priorities and structure your work toward clear goals. No ticket queue, no micromanagement.

Our product sits at the boundary between algorithms, software systems, and real industrial operations.

We care about building systems that are easy to integrate, responsive, understandable, and maintainable as both the product and the underlying algorithms evolve.

We use GenAI extensively to prototype, implement, and explore alternatives. But generating code is not the hard part. The value lies in designing the right system, choosing good abstractions, validating behavior, and knowing what is worth building.

  • Fluent English. German and experience in manufacturing or industrial planning are useful but not required.

      • Lead external level design contractors and outsourcing partners by providing clear briefs, regular feedback and quality reviews, ensuring all delivered content meets Treefrog’s standards.

    Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

    We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

    Here’s what this particular role covers.

    🛠️ About our Verification and Release Test Team

    Wayve’s Verification and Release Test team sits at the intersection of hardware, embedded software and machine learning models. Our testing spans component, system and vehicle levels, and we build novel test automation in-house to identify issues earlier in development. We pride ourselves on finding the most efficient and effective ways to deliver the most valuable results for the company.

    As a System Test Engineer, HIL, you’ll build robust, reusable automation and work across engineering disciplines to improve coverage, reliability and traceability. This is a hands-on delivery role with room to grow into broader areas of the system, including sensing and model-behaviour testing, as Wayve and your experience evolve.

    🧠 Your day-to-day

    • Develop automation for system functionality tests at component, integration and system levels, working across software and hardware boundaries.

    • Lead root-cause investigations for failures identified during test campaigns, collaborating with hardware, software, infrastructure and DevOps teams to resolve issues.

    • Analyse test results, uncover software and hardware bugs, and report findings through Jira with clear evidence to support debugging.

    • Optimise Buildkite CI/CD-integrated test workflows for rapid, reliable and repeatable execution.

    • Review, create and follow risk assessments to ensure all testing activities are conducted safely and responsibly.

    🧩 What you’ll be working on:

    • Independently owning the design and delivery of automated verification for a defined area of our embedded software stack, steadily raising the bar on coverage, reliability and traceability.

    • Building open-loop and closed-loop hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) replay tests, alongside reliability and fault-injection tests, to support verification, release and debugging.

    • Automating HIL test setups and improving test infrastructure to expand coverage, make failures easier to trace and strengthen compliance reporting.

    • Integrating requirements, coverage and compliance workflows, including Jama, MC/DC coverage analysis and MISRA checks, and managing test artefacts through Artifactory and Azure.

    • Developing traceability dashboards and defining KPIs and quality metrics that support data-driven validation and release decisions.

    🙌 You should apply if:

    • You have hands-on experience with system-level verification and validation in robotics, embedded software or mechatronic systems, with a track record of independently delivering test automation.

    • You’re highly proficient in Python and have experience developing automation test frameworks using pytest.

    • You’ve worked with HIL testing and tooling, including interfaces such as CAN, Ethernet or GMSL, and tools from dSPACE, Vector, Xylon or similar providers.

    • You understand open-loop and closed-loop HIL replay testing using dSPACE or other emulators.

    • You’re familiar with automotive safety and process standards, including ISO 26262, ASPICE and SOTIF, and have experience integrating requirements and test-management tools such as Jama and Xray.

    • You’re proficient in CI/CD principles and related tooling, such as GitLab CI, Buildkite and Bazel.

    • You have experience developing or testing automotive software at embedded and system levels, including hardware/software interactions and interface-level testing, and have worked with L2+ hands-off, L3 or L4 automated driving systems.

    • You have knowledge of consumer safety-rating protocols such as Euro NCAP, including AEB and LSS/LKA scenarios; DCAS regulatory testing under UN R171; and automotive cybersecurity testing and standards, including ISO/SAE 21434 and UN R155.

    • You’ve worked with test automation dashboards, logging and reporting infrastructure, using tools such as Grafana, Looker, Datadog and Jira.

    • You’re a self-starter with a sharp eye for improvement who communicates clearly and works effectively across software, hardware, autonomy, DevOps and product teams.

    • Ideally, you’ve contributed to improvements in test methods, safety procedures or operational efficiency, and are familiar with data management and version control tools such as Git.

    • Experience using agentic AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code to accelerate and improve test development, debugging and automation workflows would also be valuable.

    🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

    More about Wayve:

    🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

    Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

    How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

    Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

    🔍 The Interview Process:

    Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

    • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)

    • Competency Interviews (Programming and hiring manager interview; 1 hour 45 minutes total)

    • Deep-dive technical interviews (Cross-functional, system design; 1 hour 45 minutes total)

    • Final interview: mission & values alignment (45 minutes).

    We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

    What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

    💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
    ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
    📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
    🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

    A quick, honest note before you apply.

    Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

    If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

    Why Socure?

    Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

    We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

    As an International Data Acquisition Manager at Socure, you will be instrumental in expanding and managing our global data assets to power Socure’s identity verification, fraud prevention, and compliance solutions. Your primary focus will be sourcing, evaluating, onboarding, and managing third-party data providers across international markets, with a strong emphasis on data quality, operational scalability, and regulatory compliance.

     

    Reporting to the Head of Data Acquisition and Strategy, you will collaborate closely with the Product, Data Science, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and external data partners. Together, you will identify and operationalize data sources to enhance product performance, broaden geographic reach, and drive Socure’s international growth.

     

    This role is especially critical as Socure deepens its international investments, building in-region capabilities and expanding its product support in the EU, UK, LATAM, and other key markets.

     

    What You'll Do

    Vendor and Data Management

    • Support the evaluation, onboarding, and ongoing management of third-party data vendors across multiple international markets and product lines, ensuring alignment with business priorities and needs.

    • Assist in preparing RFIs, RFPs, diligence materials, and vendor assessments to evaluate provider capabilities, data quality, compliance posture, operational fit, and commercial value.

    • Maintain clear, auditable documentation regarding purchased data, vendor status, usage rights, contractual constraints, and performance across the data acquisition lifecycle.

    • Help manage renewals and identify new vendors to improve product quality, expand coverage, and enhance cost efficiency.

     

    Collaboration and Internationalization Strategy

    • Research and evaluate new international data sources aligned with Socure’s strategic priorities, particularly for identity verification, fraud prevention, KYC/eKYC, Document Verification, and compliance use cases.

    • Develop a deep understanding of Socure products and international scenarios to assess the relevance, incremental value, and risks of potential data sources.

    • Partner with Product, Data Science, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and Procurement to align on priorities, plan integrations, and ensure effective operationalization of new data sources.

    • Contribute to data acquisition that promotes inclusivity, coverage, and fairness in identity verification across diverse populations and regions.

    • Represent the Data Acquisition team in cross-functional meetings, clearly communicating findings, trade-offs, and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

    Data Quality and Integration

    • Assist in due diligence for prospective data sources, including data quality assessments, overlap and coverage analysis, compliance reviews, and performance testing.

    • Support structured evaluations and proof-of-concept testing for new vendors and datasets using evidence-based methods to determine business value and product impact.

    • Monitor and report on data quality metrics, vendor performance, feed reliability, and issues such as drift, schema changes, or outages; help coordinate remediation as necessary.

    • Work with internal technical teams to plan integrations, including understanding schemas, APIs, delivery models, and operational dependencies.

    The role

    We’re building the AI platform freight forwarders rely on. We started with quoting and are expanding across the shipment lifecycle. As Product Lead, you will be central to that expansion, helping decide where we focus and turning those decisions into products customers depend on.

    What you’ll do:

    • Own product outcomes: Own the roadmap, priorities and performance of specific products, from defining the customer problem through launch, rollout and adoption. Partner with the founders on overall product direction and strategy.

    • Build from customer insight: Work closely with freight forwarders across commercial and operational roles. Understand how they work, identify the problems customers share and build products for those needs rather than one-off solutions.

    • Prototype and build: Turn ideas into working prototypes and early product versions, using AI tools and code to test them with customers. Work hands-on with engineering to take promising ideas into production, not just write specs and hand them over.

    • Drive product expansion: Build a clear view of the market, including where we win, where we do not compete and why customers choose us. Use that understanding to identify the next workflows Nexcade should enter and turn them into products that grow revenue.

    • Raise the standard of product thinking: Define success measures, test assumptions and examine accuracy, edge cases and second-order effects before scaling. Write clear specs and decision documents, including a written recommendation on the hard calls.

    • Build the product operating system: Establish a clear planning and decision-making cadence without adding bureaucracy. Make sure product meetings are well prepared, teams have the context they need and decisions translate into shipped work.

    • Make product and platform trade-offs: Work closely with engineering to decide when to invest in shared capabilities and when a faster, product-specific approach is right.

    What we look for

    • Strong product judgement: You have owned meaningful product work in a complex B2B product and can show how your decisions changed customer behaviour or business results. You define success clearly and test assumptions, accuracy and edge cases before scaling.

    • Product taste: You can turn complex workflows into products that feel simple, coherent and trustworthy. You care about the details that make people choose to use them.

    • Technical fluency: You work effectively with strong engineers, understand trade-offs across architecture, AI, data and integrations and bring the customer and product perspective to choices about speed, quality and reuse.

    • Excellent judgement: You get beyond what customers ask for to understand how their work really happens and distinguish repeatable needs from bespoke requests. You use customer and market insight to make product choices that drive adoption, expansion and revenue.

    • High agency and directness: You take ownership, hold a high bar and disagree openly and constructively. You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast iteration and changing priorities.

    • Obsess over the problem: You are drawn to complex, messy problems in industries the economy depends on and want to understand how the people and systems behind them really work. Industry experience is a bonus, but not required.

    Why join

    The biggest product choices are still ahead: how deep we go, where we expand and how everything fits together. Our product is already live with leading freight forwarders and this role will shape what comes next. You will build AI for the work that keeps global trade moving, alongside a team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will get meaningful equity in the company you help build.

    About Flock

    Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

    We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

    We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

     

    About the role

    Reporting to Sarah Phillips, you’ll own month-end for Flock’s finance team and strengthen the controls around it, running the close and producing the variance analysis and MI that FP&A and our senior team use for budgeting and reporting. We’re automating finance on our new platform and the team uses AI every day, so there’s plenty of room to improve how the work gets done as well as doing it.

    It suits a recently qualified accountant with strong core accounting from practice, who has already improved a process or control somewhere and wants to keep growing within the finance team.

     

    What you’ll be doing

    • Own the month-end close from start to finish so it lands accurately and on time.

    • Prepare balance sheet reconciliations and post journals, keeping the ledger clean and well evidenced.

    • Run variance analysis and build the monthly MI pack, explaining what moved and why.

    • Strengthen our financial controls and automate manual steps wherever you find them.

    • Prepare our VAT returns and assist with group reporting.

    • Work with FP&A so the numbers behind budgets and senior reporting are right.

    • Support the annual audit and work alongside our external auditors.

    • Use AI tools in your daily work to speed up reconciliations, analysis and reporting, and share what works with the team.

    About Kestra

    Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

    Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

    About the role

    Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
    You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
    This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
    This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one.

    What you would do

    Your first six months would focus on the first three points below. The rest is where the role grows.

    • Conduct hands-on penetration testing and threat modeling across our web application, APIs, control plane, and cloud environments.

    • Manage end-to-end vulnerability tracking across our codebases, software dependencies (SCA), container images, and cloud infrastructure.

    • Proactively fix security flaws by writing patches, submitting Pull Requests (PRs), or collaborating directly with product teams to guide remediation.

    • Audit and harden our cloud infrastructure (GCP, Kubernetes clusters, and networking configurations) against external and internal threats.

    • Automate security tooling into our CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, dependency scanners) to catch CVEs before code reaches production.

    • Perform security code reviews and evaluate third-party dependencies, open-source integrations, and supply-chain risks.

    • Lead incident response efforts and establish continuous monitoring, detection, and mitigation strategies.

    • Own our public security posture as an open-source project: vulnerability disclosure process, CVE handling, security advisories, and the trust model of our plugin ecosystem.

    Our Tech Stack

    • Security & Vulnerability Tools: Trivy, GitHub Security / Dependabot, Elastic Security

    • Infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

    • Cloud: GCP

    • Programming language: Java, Typescript, Javascript

    • Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

    • Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

    • Monitoring & Logs: ELK, Prometheus, Grafana

    • Deployment & Repository: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

    What we are looking for

    • 5+ years of experience in Security Engineering, Product Security, DevSecOps, or a combined Offensive/Defensive role.

    • Strong hands-on penetration testing background, with proven ability to discover application, API, and network-level vulnerabilities.

    • A builder/fixer mindset: You don't just export scanner PDFs; you can read code, understand exploits, write fixes, or provide clear remediation steps to engineers.

    • Deep familiarity with cloud security (AWS or GCP) and containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker).

    • Experience with dependency and supply-chain security (CVE management, open-source licensing, SCA tools).

    • Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

    • Adaptability to a fast-paced open-source startup environment where pragmatism and execution speed matter.

    Perks & Benefits

    • Work from anywhere: We’re a remote-first company, so you can work from wherever feels like home. Plus, you’ll have access to coworking spaces worldwide if you ever need a change of scenery.

    • Health coverage: From medical support, dental, and vision, we've got you covered.

    • Home office setup on us: We’ll provide all the equipment you need to work comfortably.

       

    Our Hiring Process

    We aim to move quickly (2-3 weeks), but we can adjust the timeline if needed.

    • Intro call with the hiring manager (30 min)

    • Technical scenario / Practical assessment (2 hours, asynchronous homework focusing on threat assessment and remediation)

    • Team chat with one of your future colleagues (30 min)

    • Final discussion with one of our co-founders (30 min)

    • Ship the golden paths so the safe way is the easy one.

    • Harden security across our cloud native ecosystem (AWS and GCP) and third-party providers.

    • Own access management from onboarding to offboarding, and get it to the point where it runs without you.

    • Prioritize vulnerability findings by real exposure, assign them to the team that owns the code, and follow remediation through to closure.

    • Own security incident response from detection through resolution.

    • Turn manual processes into pipelines that run on their own.

    • Launch and run Vibe's private bug bounty program.

    • Own SOC 2 compliance end to end and maintain current certification.

    • Drive Vibe's future compliance initiatives and requirements.

    • Define Vibe's security posture and make it self-serve so enterprise deals clear security without routing through you.

    Contexte scientifique et objectifs du stage :

    Des dispositifs d’électronique organique ultra-flexibles, conformables et implantables incorporant une intelligence artificielle promettent de révolutionner la surveillance et le traitement en temps réel de maladies chroniques [1]. De tels systèmes pourraient être basés sur des transistors organiques électrochimiques (OECTs), exploitant des conducteurs polymères mixtes ion-électron (PMIECs) comme couches actives. En effet, les PMIECs sont apparus comme une excellente plateforme matérielle pour interfacer la biologie avec l’électronique conventionnelle ; identifié comme le domaine de la « bioélectronique organique ou plastique ». L’OECT est considéré comme l’éléments clé pour réaliser une telle interface [2]. Son efficacité est évaluée suivant des figures de mérite (FoMs) telles que i) la transconductance (gm), et/ou ii) les temps de commutation (ionique vs. électronique) dans le dispositif. Au-delà des applications de transduction, à court terme, l’OECT est aussi intéressant pour créer des applications émergentes en matière de circuits neuromorphiques bioélectroniques [3].

    La réalisation de tels circuits est freinée par un manque de compréhension et d’optimisation des processus de conduction mixte dans ces matériaux polymériques ; notamment une asymétrie des temps de commutation des transistors lors des séquences de dopage (i.e « ON ») vs dédopage (i.e « OFF ») dans le canal de l’OECT. Des outils de caractérisation in-situ & operando permettant de quantifier et cartographier les paramètres de transduction électronique et électrochimique dans le canal de l’OECT se révèlent être indispensables pour comprendre les limitations actuelles en performances des PMIECs et/ou pour construire des PMIECs optimums dans de tels circuits neuromorphiques.

     

    Dans ce contexte scientifique, le.la stagiaire développera une nouvelle mesure de spectroscopie et instrumentation d’optique non linéaire, appelée microscopie par génération de second harmonique résolue en temps, afin d’enregistrer le mouvement spatio-temporel des espèces chargées, ion et électrons (ou trous), et ainsi donc cartographier les mobilités électroniques in-situ & operando le canal de l’OECT.

    La.le stagiaire fabriquera ces dispositifs OECTs en salle blanche de microélectronique, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement technique pour leur réalisation. Il.elle enregistrera et analysera les FoMs clés grâce à l'expérimentation d’optique non linéaire développée et aux caractérisations électriques et électrochimiques afin d’établir, de manière plus globale, des règles d’ingénierie dans ces PMIECs qui serviront de socle de connaissances incontournables à l’avenir, pour mettre en œuvre et appliquer des circuits neuromorphiques à base d'OECTs, comme première brique d’une intelligence artificielle d’électronique organique.

    The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) applications across cloud and edge environments is driving the need for highly efficient hardware capable of supporting increasingly demanding workloads. Among these, matrix multiplication – particularly General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) – remains the dominant computational kernel in modern AI models, including deep neural networks and transformer architectures. Conventional electronic accelerators, while highly optimized, face growing challenges related to energy consumption, data movement, and scalability.

    Silicon photonics has emerged as a promising technology to address these limitations by enabling highbandwidth, low-latency, and potentially energy-efficient computation through optical signal processing. In particular, recent advances in photonic computing leveraging phase-change materials (PCM) offer new opportunities for implementing reconfigurable and non-volatile computational primitives directly in the optical domain.

    This PhD is part of the CAMELIA program (ASIC and Numérique agencies) within the targeted project LEAF, and aims to explore a hybrid photonic–electronic computing paradigm for AI acceleration. The central objective is to design and evaluate silicon photonics-based architectures for efficient GEMM operations, building on recent work demonstrating a reconfigurable photonic GEMM architecture based on PCM and stochastic computing.

    The proposed research will focus on extending this tile-based photonic GEMM approach toward large-scale matrix operations under realistic conditions. Key challenges include managing PCM-related constraints such as limited precision and quantization effects, mitigating noise and variability, and addressing interface latency between photonic and electronic domains.

    A major aspect of the PhD will be the development of system-level evaluation and benchmarking methodologies within a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO/SDTCO) framework. The objective is to provide quantitative and objective metrics for decision-making, including scalability analysis, computational throughput, and energy efficiency for target AI workloads. These evaluations will support both intermediate design exploration and the potential experimental validation of fabricated demonstrators within the broader program.

    In addition, the PhD will address electronic circuit design challenges associated with photonic accelerators, including interface circuits for control, programming of PCM elements, optical-to-electrical readout, and signal conversion. These aspects are critical for ensuring the practical integration of photonic computing units within heterogeneous AI hardware systems.

    The expected outcome is a set of novel architectures, models, and evaluation tools that will clarify the potential and limitations of silicon photonics for next-generation AI accelerators, and provide guidelines for scalable and energy-efficient implementations.


    Background: The candidate should hold or be about to obtain an MSc in Electronics Engineering, Photonics, or Computer Engineering. A strong background in computer architecture, integrated circuits, or photonic systems is expected. Knowledge of AI hardware accelerators, in-memory computing, or silicon photonics will be appreciated.

    Environment: The PhD will be carried out at the INL laboratory, within the CAMELIA program, as part of the LEAF project, in collaboration between leading academic and institutional partners in AI hardware and photonics.

    Starting dates: Fall 2026

    About ElevenLabs

    ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

    We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

    We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

    • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

    • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

    • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

    Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

    How we work

    • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

    • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

    • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

    • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

    • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

    What we offer

    • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

    • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

    • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

    • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

    • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

    • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

    About the role

    We're looking for an experienced, driven Strategic Account Executive to drive ElevenLabs' growth across Switzerland's largest enterprises. Our ideal candidate has a well-established network and a proven track record of selling to C-level and senior decision-makers at major Swiss brands and is passionate about the transformative possibilities of AI voice technology.

    In this role you'll act as a strategic partner and trusted advisor, enabling clients to leverage our industry-leading models and ElevenAgents — our end-to-end platform for building and deploying AI voice agents — to reimagine their customer experience, internal workflows, and monetization strategies.

    In this role you will:

    • Build and manage a growing portfolio of strategic accounts across Switzerland to help ElevenLabs meet its revenue goals.

    I. CONTEXT

    Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organisation providing emergency assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters, based solely on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

    MSF International is the legal entity whose membership is composed of all MSF associations. It hosts the International Secretariat, supports the International Board, facilitates coordination across the MSF movement, and provides shared services and initiatives as mandated by the movement.

    Within MSF International, the International Office acts as the Secretariat of the International Board (IB) and operates under the direct management of the International Secretary General (ISG).     The MSF International Managing Director is a senior executive role responsible for institutional leadership, stewardship of resources, and organizational performance of MSF International as a legal entity serving the MSF movement.

    The role ensures that MSF International:

    • Effectively implements -within the scope of MSF International - the MSF International Multiyear Plan and SPARC (MSF-wide Strategic Planning, Accountability and Resource Cycle) and supports the International Board and the International Secretary General in their governance roles and responsibilities.

    • Provides high quality, well governed services to the MSF movement, as mandated by the Full ExCom (executive committee);

    • Operates with strong systems of governance, accountability, risk management and duty of care;

    • Has robust, transparent and efficient governance, financial, human, and knowledge systems;

    • Operates as a coherent, inclusive, and accountable internationally distributed organization;

In multidisciplinaire teams werk je samen met onder andere softwareontwikkelaars, domeinexperts en toekomstige eindgebruikers aan innovatieve oplossingen voor nationale en internationale stakeholders. Je bent hiervoor bereid om te reizen naar verschillende locaties, voornamelijk binnen Nederland.

    Wat breng je mee?

    Je bent iemand die in kansen denkt en nieuwsgierig is om bij te dragen aan oplossingen die werken in de praktijk. Je hebt heel makkelijk contact met eindgebruikers en kan hun wensen en ideeën snel in creatieve implementaties omzetten. Met je creatieve instelling maak je nieuwe technieken snel eigen en weet je deze te vertalen naar concrete resultaten!

    Daarnaast:

    • Heb je een afgeronde bachelor of master opleiding in ICT, Computer Science, Informatica, Informatiekunde, of vergelijkbaar;

    • Heb je minstens 8 jaar relevante werkervaring, waarvan minstens 5 jaar ervaring op het gebied van netwerktechnologie, TCP/UDP, netwerkprotocollen, routering, switching en netwerkbeveiliging;

    • Beheers je meerdere programmeertalen zoals C, C++, C#, Java en ervaring in scripting om experimenteeromgevingen snel op te zetten of aan te passen;

    • Heb je interesse in experimenteren, wargaming en simulatie in een R&D-context;

    • Heb je ervaring met het ontwerpen en beheren van robuuste, schaalbare netwerkomgevingen;

    • Ben je bereid om je te verdiepen in (militaire) luchtvaartoperaties;

    • Werk je graag samen, durft je te experimenteren en kan je technische keuzes uitleggen aan niet-technische collega’s;

    • Kan jij je in de Nederlandse en Engelse taal zowel mondeling als schriftelijk uitstekend uitdrukken.

    Nice to have:

    • Ervaring met of interesse in simulatie- en interoperabiliteitsprotocollen (DIS/HLA/FOMs);

    • Ervaring met het opzetten van tijdelijke of experimentele infrastructuren;

    • Kennis van netwerkbeveiliging of VPN-oplossingen;

    • Ervaring met monitoring- of observabilitytools;

    • Interesse in nieuwe technologieën zoals autonome systemen, AI in simulatie of digitale twins.

    Wat bieden wij jou?

    Werken bij NLR, betekent werken in een nationale en internationale hightech omgeving. Samenwerken en betrokkenheid staan bij ons hoog in vaandel. Door jou vrijheid en eigen verantwoordelijkheid te geven, ben jij het best in staat om tot baanbrekende innovaties te komen. Wil jij jezelf vakinhoudelijk én op persoonlijk vlak ontwikkelen? Ook dat kan bij NLR als lerende organisatie, met daarnaast een opleidingsbudget, een mentor, interne coaches en goede contacten met mbo’s, hbo’s en universiteiten.

    Naast dit alles bieden wij jou:

    • De kans om bij te dragen aan complexe en maatschappelijk relevante vraagstukken;

    • Een bruto maandsalaris tussen € 4330,- en € 7000,- (bij fulltime dienstverband), afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring;

    • 45 verlofdagen (bij fulltime dienstverband);

    • 8% vakantiegeld én een vaste eindejaarsuitkering van 8%;

    • De kosten voor reizen met het openbaar vervoer worden volledig vergoed. Reis je met eigen vervoer? Dan ontvang je een kilometervergoeding voor woon-werkverkeer;

    • Een zorgtoelage via onze collectieve zorgverzekering bij OHRA als extra ondersteuning voor jouw zorgkosten;

    • Extra betaald ouderschapsverlof;

    • Een goede pensioenregeling

    Jouw nieuwe werkomgeving

    Bij de afdeling Training & Simulatie werken op dit moment rond de 100 deskundigen op het gebied van simulatie, informatica, training, luchtvaart en psychologie. Binnen onze projecten wordt multidisciplinair samengewerkt, zowel binnen als buiten het NLR. De afdeling beschikt over allerlei onderzoeksfaciliteiten zoals een battlelab en simulatoren voor gevechtsvliegtuig- en onbemande systemen en een laboratorium dat zich richt op AR/VR innovaties. Een plezierige werkomgeving vinden we essentieel. De sfeer binnen de afdeling is informeel en collegiaal en we vinden het belangrijk dat iedereen zich thuis kan voelen bij ons.

    Wat betekent werken bij NLR?

    Koninklijke NLR is al ruim 100 jaar een kennisorganisatie met de wil en ambitie om te vernieuwen. Vanuit die drijfveer maken wij de wereld van lucht- en ruimtevaart veiliger, duurzamer, efficiënter en effectiever en staan wij voor baanbrekende innovaties.

    Bij ons werken bijna 1000 gedreven professionals, van vliegtuigbouwkundigen tot psychologen en van wiskundigen tot applicatiedeskundigen. NLR staat voor een inclusieve en diverse organisatie waar iedereen zich welkom, veilig, gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelt.

    Mooi, we zijn benieuwd naar jou! Stuur je motivatiebrief en CV via de ‘Solliciteren’ button.

     

    Een positieve uitkomst van een veiligheidsonderzoek (VGB) is een voorwaarde voor indiensttreding. Meer informatie daarover lees je op de website van de MIVD.

    If you are the kind of person who is not satisfied until an automated system actually works reliably, not just once, this internship is designed for you.

    We are looking for a Robot Programming & Automation Intern to help build the software behind our robotic test and automation infrastructure. Your first project is turning a robotic arm on a linear rail into a system that reliably captures good calibration data — but the skills involved are the same ones we’ll lean on for whatever we automate next: getting a robot to move well, knowing whether the data it’s collecting is any good, and building something solid enough to run unattended.

    Getting that right is the substance of this internship, on this project and on whatever comes after it.

    What you’ll do

    • Build the robot control layer: drive the arm through its SDK, coordinate the linear rail, and plan safe motion inside a cell that also has a target, cables, and an operator in it.

    • Design pose generation that’s actually informed by the calibration problem, including getting proper coverage across a multi-camera rig rather than just one lens at a time.

    • Get the timing and synchronisation right between the robot, the cameras, and the captured data — this is where automated rigs usually go wrong.

    • Gate data quality at capture time, and retry within the run rather than finding out later that a dataset is unusable.

    • Close the loop with our existing calibration pipeline: feed it data, read back its results, and use that to decide what to capture next and when a run is done.

    • Package captures with the metadata needed to make a calibration reproducible, and make the whole thing robust to failures mid-run.

    • Build a simple operator-facing workflow: mount the rig, pick a profile, press go.

    • Work closely with the mechanical intern — your requirements shape their fixture design, and their measurements shape your motion limits.

There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

    Company Operating Rhythm

    At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

    Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

    Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

    The Opportunity

    Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.


    The Role

    As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

    • Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

    • Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

    • Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

    • Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.  Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives.   

    • Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.

    1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations

    Mastery of Core Concepts

    Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways

    Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.

    Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing

    2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation

    Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks

    Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.

    Turning Theory into Practice

    Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.

    Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source

    Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.


    3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems

    Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines

    Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains.     Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.


    5. Rigorous Experimental Design

    Controlled Comparisons & Ablations

    Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.

    From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.

      About Us

      Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

      About the role

      Every airframe Harmattan AI flies starts with a model. System identification turns flight data into the verified dynamics that guidance and control are designed, tuned and trained on. It is the foundation of an autopilot that adapts across multirotors, fixed wings, VTOLs and missiles.

      As a System Identification Engineer, working out of Lausanne, you will own the path from flight test to identified model. You will design and run your own experiments, build a repeatable identification pipeline, and deliver models the G&C team can trust.

       
       

      Responsibilities

      • Experiment Design & Flight Test: Plan and run your own identification tests, from excitation design to flight tests, including coordinating with the .

      • Model Identification: Identify rigid-body, aerodynamic, propulsion and actuator dynamics using frequency and time-domain methods, including closed-loop identification on vehicles flown under a controller.

      • Propulsion & Actuators: Characterize motors, ESCs, propellers and control surfaces, including bandwidth, delays, saturation, and thermal and battery effects.

      • Identification Pipeline: Build and maintain an automated, reproducible pipeline from flight logs to identified model. This covers ingestion, data-quality checks, estimation, validation and reporting.

      • Model Validation: Validate models against held-out flight data, quantify uncertainty, and make sure each model is fit for purpose: controller design, simulation, or training learned G&C.

      • New Airframes: Extend the capability from multirotors to control-surface multirotors, fixed wings, tail-sitters and missiles.

      • Simulation & G&C Support: Deliver models into simulation, SITL and HITL, and work closely with control, guidance and embedded engineers to close the loop between models and flight results.

      • Mentorship: Depending on seniority, support the team by mentoring junior engineers and interns.

       
       

      Candidate Requirements

      • Educational Background: A strong academic record with a degree in aerospace, control, mechanical engineering or a related STEM field. A practical track record matters more than the specific degree.

      • System Identification: Proven experience identifying dynamic models of flying platforms from real data, in both the frequency and time domain, including the pitfalls of closed-loop data.

      • Flight Mechanics & Control: Solid grasp of rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamic forces and moments, non-dimensionalization, stability modes and propulsion models. Also enough control background to know what the model will be used for.

      • Flight Testing: Hands-on experience planning and running flight tests and working from raw, imperfect logs.

      • Software: Strong Python and scientific computing skills, with the discipline to build tools others can rerun.

       

      Nice to have

      • Rigorous about data quality, uncertainty and validation; skeptical of models until they are proven.

      • Autonomous and hands-on, comfortable moving between bench, field and code.

      • Fixed-wing aerodynamic modeling; VTOL or tail-sitter dynamics; remote pilot certification; experience with real flight logs; structural or vibration modes; data-driven or learned dynamics models.

      • Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission of providing a defensive edge to allied nations through ethical, high-impact technology.

      We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

      Geef je carrière een vliegende start

      MVRDV is een wereldwijd gerenommeerd architectuur- en stedenbouwkundig bureau met het hoofdkantoor in Rotterdam en kantoren in Shanghai, Parijs, Berlijn en New York. MVRDV werd in 1993 opgericht door Winy Maas, Jacob van Rijs en Nathalie de Vries en zet zich in voor het ontwerpen van innovatieve, maatschappelijk verantwoorde en duurzame architectuur die de toekomst vormgeeft.

      Als stagiair bij MVRDV maak je deel uit van een energiek, internationaal team van meer dan 200 professionals uit ruim 40 verschillende landen. Je doet praktijkervaring op in baanbrekende projecten, werkt samen met toonaangevende architecten en verlegt de grenzen van ontwerp en innovatie. Ben jij gepassioneerd over architectuur en wil je leren in een dynamische en creatieve omgeving? Dan horen we graag van je.

      Let op: We verzoeken recruitmentbureaus vriendelijk om geen ongevraagde kandidaten of profielen voor deze vacature aan te leveren. Wij verzorgen het wervingsproces intern en accepteren geen voorwaarden of vergoedingen met betrekking tot ongevraagde doorverwijzingen.

      Sollicitatieprocedure

      1. Je kunt je sollicitatie indienen vanaf nu tot en met 16 november 2026.

      2. De gesprekken vinden plaats tussen 23 november en 11 december 2026.

      3. Succesvolle kandidaten starten op 1 maart 2027.

      Belangrijk: Om in aanmerking te komen voor deze stage moet je gedurende de volledige stageperiode, van 1 maart 2027 tot en met 31 augustus 2027, ingeschreven blijven staan aan een daarvoor in aanmerking komende opleiding aan een universiteit of hogeschool.

      Over het Design Collective

      Het Design Collective van MVRDV is verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen van innovatieve en duurzame gebouwen en constructies. We werken aan een breed scala aan projecten, van kleinschalige woningbouw tot grootschalige commerciële en culturele complexen. Bekijk enkele voorbeelden van onze projecten op: https://www.mvrdv.com/projects.

      Het Design Collective richt zich op projecten in de volgende regio’s:

      • Nederland

      • Azië

      • DACH-regio

      • Franstalige landen

      • Noord-Amerika

      • Centraal- en Oost-Europa

      • Taiwan

      • Midden-Oosten

      Over de functie

      Als Architectuurstagiair bij MVRDV kom je terecht in een dynamische omgeving waar gedurfde ideeën en snel schakelen dagelijks centraal staan. Je wordt begeleid door internationaal vooraanstaande ontwerpers bij projecten en prijsvragen en levert een bijdrage aan ambitieuze concepten, gedetailleerde tekeningen en indrukwekkende visualisaties.

      Afhankelijk van jouw profiel en ervaring word je gekoppeld aan specifieke projecten, regio’s en/of projecttypen.

      Dit is een uitstekende kans om je vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen, je creativiteit uit te dagen en een realistisch beeld te krijgen van het werken aan de voorhoede van de architectuur.

      Wat ga je doen?

      • Assisteren bij de ontwikkeling van concepten en ontwerpvoorstellen.

      • Maken van tekeningen, diagrammen en 3D-modellen.

      • Ontwikkelen van visualisaties en presentatiemateriaal voor prijsvragen en opdrachtgevers.

      • Deelnemen aan teamoverleggen en ontwerpbesprekingen.

      • Onderzoek doen naar materialen, locatieomstandigheden en architectonische referenties.

      Wat bieden wij?

      Leren van marktleiders

      Word onderdeel van een wereldwijd, ambitieus en optimistisch team dat werkt aan architectonische en stedenbouwkundige vraagstukken over de hele wereld. Je werkt samen met professionals uit verschillende disciplines, van ontwerp tot business support.

      Stagevergoeding

      Je ontvangt een aantrekkelijke stagevergoeding van €1.100 per maand, plus een vergoeding voor je woon-werkverkeer (via een NS-Business Card of kilometervergoeding).

      For this role, we will only consider candidates who are currently based in the Netherlands.

      About SkinVision

      Skin cancer is highly treatable when caught early, but limited access to specialist care and long wait times delay diagnosis, increasing the risk of late-stage cases and driving up treatment costs. SkinVision, founded in Amsterdam in 2012, exists to close that gap. Our proprietary AI — certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU regulation, with over 90% sensitivity and 89% specificity — has already helped nearly 3 million people worldwide detect early signs of skin cancer. Today, SkinVision has a database of more than 6 million skin spot assessments and can reach 20 million people through insurer partnerships. High-risk cases are reviewed by a team of dermatologists, who support users in taking the right next step — from urgent care to a specialist referral. We are extending this further, connecting users faster to the specialist care they need. We're a focused, international team, active globally, united by one goal: making early detection accessible to everyone, everywhere. If you join us, you're not just building a product — you're helping close the gap between a person noticing something and getting the care they need.

      DevOps at SkinVision

      As a DevOps Engineer at SkinVision, you will play a key role in building, scaling, and securing the infrastructure that powers our AI-driven health platform. You’ll design and maintain our cloud-based systems in AWS, implement CI/CD pipelines, enhance observability using Datadog, and drive operational excellence through automation and monitoring.

      Your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of a medical-grade system that serves users globally. You’ll collaborate closely with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure smooth delivery, rapid deployments, and resilient operations — ultimately enabling us to deliver life-saving technology with confidence.

      Beyond hands-on expertise with AWS and modern DevOps tooling, we’re looking for someone who thinks architecturally. You’ll get to know our current setup, form your own view of how it should evolve, and help define a target vision for our infrastructure, then drive its implementation. Day-to-day operational work is part of the role, but we value someone who thinks before building and takes ownership of where our infrastructure goes next.

      What you will do

      Cloud Infrastructure & Automation

      • Design, build, and manage AWS-based infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency.

      • Implement and manage infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation.

      • Automate environment provisioning, configuration, and deployments using CI/CD pipelines.

      • Ensure system resilience, security, and performance through automated monitoring and alerting.

      CI/CD & Deployment

      • Design and optimize CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, reliable, and safe deployments across environments.

      • Manage deployment workflows using Argo CD and Kubernetes.

      • Collaborate with developers and ML engineers to streamline build, test, and release processes.

      • Integrate automated testing, rollback strategies, and version control into the deployment lifecycle.

      Observability & Monitoring

      • Build a comprehensive observability stack using Datadog for metrics, logs, traces, and alerts.

      • Define service-level objectives (SLOs), service-level indicators (SLIs), and dashboards for system performance.

      • Proactively detect and resolve performance bottlenecks, capacity issues, and reliability risks.

      • Create automated health checks and ensure visibility across production systems.

      Security & Compliance

      • Implement security best practices for AWS, containers, and CI/CD pipelines.

      • Manage identity, access, and secret handling (IAM, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store).

      • Ensure compliance with medical device standards and data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA).

      • Partner with the Information Security Officer to embed security controls across infrastructure and deployments.

      Reliability & Incident Management

      • Lead incident response and root cause analysis for infrastructure or deployment-related issues.

      • Establish SLAs and operational runbooks for production environments.

      • Continuously improve system reliability through chaos testing, redundancy, and fault tolerance.

      • Mentor engineers on DevOps principles, observability practices, and infrastructure automation.

      Infrastructure Strategy & Architecture

      • Assess the current infrastructure and deployment setup, and form a well-reasoned view of how it should evolve.

      • Define and maintain a target architecture for our cloud platform, balancing reliability, scalability, security, and cost.

      • Translate the target vision into a practical roadmap and drive its implementation incrementally, alongside day-to-day operations.

      • Document and communicate architectural decisions, aligning with engineering and leadership on technical direction.


      Essential skills

      • Minimum of 6 years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Infrastructure roles.

      • Strong expertise with AWS services (EC2, ECS/EKS, S3, RDS, CloudWatch, Lambda, etc.).

      • Expert in Kubernetes and Argo CD, deploying and managing production-grade custom Helm charts with secure, automated GitOps workflows in EKS

      • Advanced knowledge of CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar).

      • Proficiency in Datadog for observability, monitoring, and alerting.

      • Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, Bash, or Go.

  2. A/R & Aging Management: Work insurance aging reports, investigate unpaid or underpaid claims, post insurance payments (EOBs/ERAs), and file appeals/reconsiderations.

  • Revenue Cycle Mastery: Hands-on experience across claims submission, ERA/EOB payment posting, denial resolution, and A/R aging follow-up.
  • Proactive Problem Solver: Self-starter mentality with the ability to take ownership of complex aging accounts without micro-supervision.
  • Remote Setup: A private, HIPAA-compliant home office with a reliable computer setup, high-speed internet, and a clear headset.

Ideal Candidate Profile

You are a tenacious, sharp dermatology biller who knows ModMed inside and out. You treat unresolved claims as personal challenges, spot coding discrepancies before submission, and keep practice revenue flowing smoothly.
